messages:
Alex G: heads-up — gpupool-us-east1b started showing 3 nodes NotReady and NoSchedule ~15m ago right after the cert rotation job ran. device-plugin logs show grpc TLS handshake failures. @Maria S can you take a look?
Maria S: on it. seeing the same in the deploy logs. autoscaler still trying to scale up but new nodes get tainted almost immediately.
Jon: leaving a note — we saw similar behavior last quarter when kubelet cert reload timing overlapped with the nvidia-device-plugin restart. could be cert rotation -> plugin restart -> plugin can't connect to kubelet because cert socket not ready.
Alex G: logs excerpt from one affected node:```stderr
E0324 14:12:07.123456 1 device_plugin.go:213] grpc: transport: authentication handshake error: remote error: tls: bad certificate
E0324 14:12:07.123789 1 device_plugin.go:217] Failed to register with kubelet: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection error: desc = "transport: authentication handshake error"
```
infra-bot: DeployJob #9245 finished: cert-rotation (success). Rolling post-hook triggered at 14:11:58
oncall-sre: quick check — are the node certs actually renewed or did they get rotated out of order? I see some nodes with expiry still far out.
Maria S: looks like the cert-rotation job rotated cluster-level certs but the node bootstrap flow that updates /var/lib/kubelet/pki/kubelet-client-current.pem lagged due to an racy systemd unit on the node. device-plugin restarted while kubelet wasn't yet presenting the new certs.
DevOps Lead: immediate mitigation options?
Jon: safe mitigations: 1) roll device-plugin DaemonSet to restart plugins after kubelet certs are refreshed (add a precheck for cert timestamp), or 2) temporarily disable autoscaler for the pool so we don't add more nodes that will taint themselves.
Maria S: doing (2) now — paused autoscaler for gpupool-us-east1b. Also applying a short patch to the device-plugin DaemonSet that adds an init script to wait for /var/lib/kubelet/pki/kubelet-client-current.pem to exist and be newer than X minutes.
Alex G: thanks. can we also cordon and drain the 3 unhealthy nodes and restart kubelet on them after cert files are in place?
oncall-sre: cordoned the three nodes (gpupool-ue1b-003..005) and kicked a kubelet restart via ssh. watching metrics.
Maria S: patch applied to DaemonSet (image: nvidia-device-plugin:v0.10.2-patch) and rolling restart started. logs are showing successful TLS handshakes now:```
I0324 14:28:45.987654 1 device_plugin.go:189] registered with kubelet via TLS, kubelet UID: 12345
```
DevOps Lead: re-enabled autoscaler once 2 nodes showed healthy. leave autoscaler paused until full pool stable?
Alex G: re-enabled but with a strict cooldown (10m) and a scale-up cap of +1 while we monitor.
Jon: root cause writeup we should add: race between cluster cert-rotation job and node-level kubelet cert refresh + device-plugin restart ordering. Short-term: init-wait for device-plugin and autoscaler cooldown. Mid-term: bake cert rotation prechecks and a daemonset rollout hook.
Maria S: filing a runbook entry and a postmortem note. I'll paste the short remediation steps in the runbook: 1) pause autoscaler for affected pool, 2) cordon/drain unhealthy nodes, 3) ensure kubelet certs present, 4) restart kubelet, 5) roll device-plugin with init-wait, 6) uncordon and monitor for 15m.
Alex G: nice. anyone see cost implications? autoscaler paused briefly saved us from spinning 4 extra preemptible GPUs that would've been wasted while tainted. rough estimate ~ $120/hr saved during the incident window.
DevOps Lead: filing follow-up ticket to add a cert-maturity check into the rotation job and to adjust node bootstrap ordering. assign to Maria + Infra Eng.
Maria S: assigned and calendared a short run to validate in staging tomorrow. planning to backport patch to older clusters.
Alex G: thanks all — closing thread when we confirm 24h stable. :thumbsup:
